Hi Marta —

Appreciate the context — and the travel note. Short answer: we can host something that works, but we should avoid the date that brackets the EU daylight-savings change (week of 3/29) because invites created before/after may flip local labels for some participants. That is often what causes the calendar confusion.

Two recommendations from our side:
1) Pick a date outside the EU DST cutover (either the week before or the week after) so all invites resolve consistently in each attendee's calendar.
2) If you must do the week of 3/29, lock to UTC times in the invite and include explicit local times in the body — and we'll send a synced calendar invite from Redwood that uses an ICS with fixed offsets.

If it's helpful I can coordinate a few narrow windows (UTC) that are friendly for US morning / EU mid-morning / APAC late afternoon.

Availability from our core demo team: Tue 3/23 after 14:00 UTC, Thu 3/25 13:00–16:00 UTC, or Mon 4/05 13:00–15:00 UTC.

Would any of these work for BrightMarket?

—Ethan
